catalog_quote: जहां स्वराघात शब्दों पर होता है, वहां बल निश्चित स्वर पर पड़ना चाहिए । अन्यथा एक ही तरह लिखे जाने वाले शब्द अपने सही अर्थ को नहीं व्यक्त कर सकते । इस प्रकार के शब्दों में स्वराघात उनके अर्थों के अनुकूल ही निर्धारित होता है, जैसे, ख'ड़ी (खड़ी), खऽड़ी (खरिया), ब'ड़ी (बड़ी), बऽड़ी (बाटिका), ला'ट (लौर्ड: वायसराय), लाऽट (हल का अगला भाग), का'ळो (काला) काऽळो (मूर्ख), खा'ल (खाल), खाऽळ (तालाब), खाण' (खाना है) खाऽण (खान), आ'णो (आना), आऽणो (ताना), क'र (टैक्स), कऽर (करना), ब'ण (बनना), बऽण (वन), आ'ग (अग्नि), आऽग (आगे) इस प्रकार के उदाहरण गढ़वाली में अनेक हैं । प्रथम वर्ग में स्वराघात प्रथम अक्षर पर है और दूसरे में अन्त्य स्वर पर । फलतः प्रथम स्वर उसमें उच्चारण में सुदीर्घ हो जाता है । ... कुछ अन्य विशेषताएं यों हैं: [१] संयुक्त व्यंजनों के पूर्व वर्ती स्वर पर बल पड़ता है, जैसे, र'ज्जा, खा'न्द, पे'न्द, मि'ट्ठो, गि'च्चो, सा'त्तू । [२] यदि तीन स्वर ध्वनियों का शब्द हो और मध्य की ध्वनि ह्रस्व हो तो स्वराघात मध्य में होता है, जैसे, बिजु'ली, बादु'ली, नक'ली, दग'ड़ी, हैंस'दी । [३] लुप्त होती अथवा हुई स्वर ध्वनि के पूर्व स्वर पर, म'नूखी, क'मल, च'ट्, अ'प्ड़ो । [४] दो अक्षर के शब्दों में स्वराघात पहले स्वर पर होता है: हौ'र (और), द'शा, आ'श, आ'म, आं'ख । [५] तीन अथवा अधिक अक्षरों के शब्दों में अन्त के तीसरे अक्षर पर स्वराघात होता है, यदि उससे पहला स्वर दीर्घ हो: बुरांश', कबिलाश', पराणी,' सुबेदार' ।

new_statements.translation: Where accent falls on words, the stress must fall on a fixed vowel; otherwise words written the same way cannot express their proper meaning ... kha'Ri (standing), kha:Ri (chalk), ... ka'lo (black), ka:lo (fool), kha'l (skin), kha:l (pond) ... In the first group the accent is on the first syllable, in the second on the final vowel. ... [1] The vowel preceding a consonant cluster/geminate bears the stress, e.g. ra'jja, kha'nd, pe'nd, mi'TTi ... [2] If a word has three vowels and the middle one is short, the accent is in the middle, e.g. biju'li, badu'li, nak'li ... [4] In words of two syllables the accent is on the first vowel: hau'r (and), da'sha, a'sh, a'm, a'nkh. [5] In words of three or more syllables the accent falls on the third syllable at the end [sic; the accent marks in the examples stand after the final syllable], if the vowel before it is long: buransh', kabilash', paraNi', subedar'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Chatak: Garhwali has dynamic word stress (with residual pitch accent used mainly at sentence level, p. 50). Stress position is lexically distinctive in a set of segmentally identical pairs (initial-stressed vs final-stressed, the unstressed first vowel of the latter being prolonged). Otherwise: stress the vowel before a geminate/cluster; disyllables stress the first syllable; trisyllables with a short medial vowel stress the medial syllable; the vowel before a syncopated vowel is stressed; in words of 3+ syllables stress goes toward the end (text: 'third akshara at the end', marks on the final) when the preceding vowel is long. Juyal 1967 (p. 96) instead says Garhwali stress hardly differs from Hindi (weak, weight/position-driven: penult stressed only when the final vowel is deletable -a; some words like dagRa carry no perceptible stress). Bhatt 1976 (p. 28) repeats only the lexical minimal pairs. Net: impressionistic, partly weight-sensitive, partly lexical, and internally ambiguous (rule 5); no modern instrumental or theoretically explicit account was found.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None of the sources mentions secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Chatak: homograph pairs whose stress is 'determined according to meaning' (kha'Ri/khaRi', ba'Ri/baRi', la'T/laT', ka'lo/kalo', kha'l/khal', khaN'/kha:N, a'No/a:No, ka'r/ka:r, ba'N/ba:N, a'g/a:g); Rawanlti-Jaunpuri and Tehri sub-dialects have markedly more musical (pitch) accent (sec. 188-189). Juyal: adjectives may shift stress to the penult for intensification (miTTho'); vocatives stress the final vowel in Garhwali.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms; Chatak explicitly separates sentence-level (pitch/'musical') accent used for question, command, surprise, entreaty etc. from word stress. Chatak's 'akshara' counts written Devanagari syllables (final inherent a included), which makes rule 5 ambiguous between antepenult and final.
new_statements.identity_note: Chatak 1959 describes Garhwali in general with 'standard' (Srinagariya/Pauri-Tehri) Garhwali as the base; he notes separately (sec. 188-189, pp. ~133) that the Rawanlti-Jaunpuri and Tehri sub-dialects have a stronger 'musical' (pitch) accent. Juyal 1967 treats Garhwali and Kumaoni (kuma1273) together as 'Madhya Pahari' but states the Garhwali facts separately. All sources are for garh1243 proper, not Jaunsari (jaun1243).

sources.note: Garhwali keeps remnants of musical (pitch) accent, mostly at sentence level; word accent is dynamic and its position distinguishes homographs (first syllable vs final vowel: kha'ri 'standing' vs khari' 'chalk', ka'lo 'black' vs kalo' 'fool', kha'l 'skin' vs khal' 'pond'..); further tendencies: vowel before a geminate/cluster is stressed; trisyllables with short medial vowel stress the medial; vowel before a syncopated vowel is stressed; disyllables stress the first vowel; words of 3+ syllables stress 'the third akshara at the end' if the preceding vowel is long (examples marked burāṃś', kabil…

sources.citation: Bhatt 'Shailesh', Haridatt. 1976. Garhwali bhasha aur uska sahitya. Lucknow: Hindi Samiti (Hindi Samiti granthamala 244). [in Hindi]. p. 28 'svaraghat'.
sources.note: p. 28: 'Accent is of two kinds, musical and dynamic. Both tendencies exist in Garhwali, but dynamic (stress) accent is especially found. Identically written words yield different meanings according to which vowel the stress falls on, e.g. kalo (black) / ka'lo (fool); khal (skin) / kha'l (pond); baRi (big) / ba'Ri (garden); khaRi (standing) / kha'Ri (chalk).' No positional rule.

In Garhwali, as in Hindi, final vowels other than a are fully pronounced, so the penultimate vowel is stressed only when the final vowel is a' (bald: stress on ba because final a drops; bal, git light stress on a, i); 4. medial a is usually lost and the preceding vowel takes the stress (kilkar).
